newsitem.title: USA: Sacramento, Calif., sells $73.7 mln arena bonds.
newsitem.headline: Sacramento, Calif., sells $73.7 mln arena bonds.

text.p: Sacramento said Friday it sold $73.7 million of bonds to refinance an arena for the National Basketball Association Kings.

Sacramento Treasurer Thomas Friery said the lease revenue bonds were issued with an initial 10-year maturity date of July 18, 2007. The city purchased a 10-year hedge from Merrill Lynch & Co, the deal's lead underwriter, to mitigate the risk of fluctuating interest rates, he said.
The bond deal will close on July 31.
"I am pleased with the bond sale in light of the complexity of the financing and the time schedule we were operating on to take advantage of declining interest rates," Friery said in a statement.
The Sacramento City Council approved the bond deal in February to keep the Kings from leaving the city.
Legal challenges, however, threatened to scuttle the arena deal, and forced the city to delay the bond sale.
In June, a Superior Court judge ruled the financing was legal, clearing the way for Sacramento to come to market this week.
With proceeds from the bond sale, the city plans to refinance more than $50 million of Arco Arena debt, where the Kings play. The remaining funds will be used to refinance other franchise debts.
Moody's Investors Service Inc and Standard & Poor's Corp assigned the bonds AAA ratings, reflecting the insurance provided by MBIA Inc.
